Certainly! Here are two hints for the given step:

Hint 1: Consider the implications of one-hot encoding categorical variables. When you one-hot encode a categorical variable with \( $$n$$ \) categories, you typically create \( $$n-1$$ \) binary columns to avoid multicollinearity. Think about how this affects the rank of the design matrix.

Hint 2: Recall that for a matrix to be invertible, it must be square and have full rank. Analyze the structure of the design matrix \(\Phi_3\) after one-hot encoding the categorical variables and determine if it meets these criteria.
